ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure there is a circle, point R is marked inside the circle as the center of the circle; from R to point S on the circle a radius is drawn, a line segment connected at point S to external point T is labeled 20, and the problem states that this line segment is tangent to the circle; another slanted line starting from R passes through the circle to T, with the part inside the circle labeled x and the outside-the-circle part to T labeled 12, so the whole segment RT = x + 12. Then reason: The radius to the point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent line, so RS is perpendicular to ST, and triangle RST is a right triangle. Its two legs are RS = x and ST = 20, and the hypotenuse is RT = x + 12. By the Pythagorean theorem, x^2 + 20^2 = (x + 12)^2. Expand: x^2 + 400 = x^2 + 24x + 144. Cancel x^2 to get 400 = 24x + 144, so 256 = 24x, x = 256/24 = 10.666.... Rounding to the nearest tenth, x = 10.7.

method.method_draft: Use the tangent-radius right triangle. From the image, identify R as the circle’s center, S as the tangency point on the circle, ST as the tangent segment labeled 20, and the slanted segment from R through the circle to T as having radius portion x inside the circle plus exterior portion 12, so RT = x + 12. From the text, use that the segment is tangent and x must be rounded to the nearest tenth. Apply the rule that a radius to a point of tangency is perpendicular to the tangent, so triangle RST is right with legs RS = x and ST = 20 and hypotenuse RT = x + 12. Set up x^2 + 20^2 = (x + 12)^2, solve for x, then round to get 10.7.
